A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CMPT research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v3 reports original CMPT results on five multimodal datasets in Tables 1–4, with additional robustness and per-class experiments in the appendix.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and reports additional alignment-loss, rank, adapter and encoder experiments, alongside feature and attention analyses.

M1.justification: The default proxy-token, alignment, gating and fusion procedure is retained. Appendices A10–A11 add implemented variants using DoRA or VeRA instead of LoRA and a SigLIP vision encoder with global attention pooling instead of CLS-based vision representations.

E1.justification: The same five datasets and application tasks are retained. v4 additionally evaluates AVE with audio or video entirely missing; v3 reported AVE results only with complete modalities. This extends input-availability coverage within an existing task.

E2.justification: Table 9 adds DoRA-based and VeRA-based CMPT comparison variants alongside the original LoRA-based model. Baseline memberships in the retained benchmark comparisons are unchanged. Newly cited MoRA is not evaluated.

E3.justification: v4 substantially expands experimental settings through alignment-weight sweeps from 0.0 to 0.5, LoRA ranks 1/2/4, rank-matched adapter comparisons, SigLIP experiments, and Base-versus-Large encoder tests. These are added evaluation configurations; the primary splits, metrics and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Sections 4.6.3–4.6.4 and Appendices A4, A8 and A10–A12 add direct alignment-loss and rank ablations, feature-space and attention analyses of successes and failures, and adapter/backbone sensitivity studies. Earlier modality-ratio and per-class analyses are retained under new numbering.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over three independent seeds in Table 1 and the modality-ratio comparison, numbered Table 6 in v3 and Table 8 in v4. No new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes CMPT's Food-101 text-only accuracy from 80.66 to 85.31 without a stated setting change. Substantial new results accompany the added analyses. For example, Table 10 newly reports AVE video-only accuracy of 84.58% with ViT versus 30.60% with SigLIP, demonstrating sensitivity to the backbone.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation in Equations 1–7 and its formal assumptions are retained. No new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation is added; the new mechanism discussions are qualitative.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same principal claims about efficient CMPT-based missing-modality robustness, competitive complete-modality performance, generalization to missing rates and broad per-class benefits.

C2.justification: Beyond v3's modality-dependence discussion, v4 adds attention-based mechanism interpretations and detailed failure explanations in Appendix A8. Appendices A11–A12 introduce substantive applicability qualifications concerning SigLIP's audio-reconstruction failures and dataset-dependent benefits or drawbacks of larger encoders.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a future-release promise with stated code availability and a concrete repository link. v4 also explicitly discloses rank-1 LoRA tuning for the baseline/dropout ablations, without establishing a changed protocol. The original hyperparameter table is retained as Table 6.

R1.justification: v4 adds discussion of MoRA in related work and citations to DoRA, VeRA and SigLIP supporting the new variants. The broader literature organization and positioning of CMPT relative to earlier missing-modality approaches remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are preserved. Local edits clarify the task loss and comparison fairness, remove a repetitive setup sentence, and update cross-references. New analyses receive additional subsections without extensive rewriting of the original narrative.

P2.justification: v4 adds five tables and four figures, introducing t-SNE plots and attention-map displays alongside the new experimental tables. Figure 1's method illustration is revised. The original performance plots are retained, with several appendix figures relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v3 lacked direct ablations of its central alignment objective and rank choice. Table 5 and Appendix A4 supply this evidence, while the new success/failure analyses and encoder experiments substantially clarify when CMPT works and where it fails, including severe SigLIP failures. Together with concrete code-access information, these additions materially strengthen experimental justification, transparency and assessment of applicability.
